source.title: On damage of interpolation to adversarial robustness in regression

record.file_problem: Full paper text is provided, including appendices; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests consequences of near or exact interpolation for neural-network training on an adversarial regression risk, using a distinct regression setting and measure from the listed classification-training versions. Its own neural-network results bear on V1's training error and early-stopping scope, and on V3's claim that early stopping can leave error while training further changes outcomes.
record.gate_note: Most interpolation risk bounds and simulation comparisons are not measurements of training classification error. The real-data neural network experiment records training error over epochs and directly reports risk changes as training error decreases. The cited literature on gradient descent reaching interpolation is prior work, not this study's result.
record.test_reason: The study uses interpolation as a premise to investigate adversarial regression risk. Its own results do not test CIFAR classification interpolation, depth degradation or shortcuts, initialization, learning-rate stability, width-dependent local minima, or batch normalization. Decreasing regression training error and worsening test robustness do not test V1 or V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. Under their nonparametric regression assumptions, the authors establish that highly interpolating estimators, including DNNs satisfying their near-interpolation condition, cannot attain the optimal minimax adversarial rate. Their Auto MPG illustration shows increasing adversarial error as training error falls and suggests stopping earlier than the epoch minimizing standard prediction error.
record.recipe_differences: The study considers nonparametric regression under future X-attacks, with minimax adversarial-risk analysis and an Auto MPG neural-network illustration; the claim versions focus mainly on classification training error and optimization recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: In the neural-network illustration, input dimension (d=2 versus d=7), epoch/early-stopping point, and adversarial radius affect the reported risk behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: On Auto MPG with d=2, standard prediction error increases from 0.595 to 0.681 between epochs 30 and 1000, while adversarial error at radius 0.1 increases from 1.313 to 3.042 as training error decreases. Relative adversarial-risk inflation is less pronounced with d=7, where additional informative features are included.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continued training can worsen adversarial regression performance as training error falls; the observed magnitude varies with the feature setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 1–5 establish an additional minimax adversarial-risk cost under interpolation constraints; Corollary 1 applies the lower bounds to DNN estimators satisfying a near-interpolation condition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the paper's nonparametric regression assumptions, sufficiently strong interpolation prevents optimal worst-case adversarial risk, even when standard-risk optimality remains possible.

record.problems: The neural-network illustration is one real-data dataset with 100 random train-test splits; the text gives limited numeric results for d=7 and does not report the training-error values at the cited epochs. It measures regression prediction risk, not classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No other numerical rows bear directly on the listed versions. The synthetic simulation compares interpolating and non-interpolating estimators on adversarial regression risk, not gradient-based training classification error.

untested.parts: All parts: convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and model-size or training-recipe qualifications.
All parts: teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and extra student neurons.
All parts: depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization or normalization exceptions.
All parts: initialization-dependent training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
All parts: recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature dynamics, edge of stability, and divergence.
All parts: batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V1 and V3 verdicts. Neither version promises adversarial robustness, and V3 makes no claim about early stopping. The theoretical results condition on interpolation rather than establish gradient-based attainment of the listed classification-training behavior.

versions.untested_parts: No CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification, random or corrupted labels, SGD or Adam comparison, width sweep, or smaller-model comparison.
No two-layer teacher-student spurious-minimum experiment or neuron-count sweep.
No depth comparison, shortcut ablation, ImageNet or CIFAR classification, or plain-network training comparison.
No initialization comparison or depth sweep.
No learning-rate stability or curvature experiment.
No batch-normalization comparison, learning-rate tolerance test, or Fixup experiment.
